[RTIM.14.11] **The `where` predicate is a real rule, and that is the whole
guarantee.** A `.dstest` `produces` assertion may carry a `where` predicate on
the `emitted` head ([LTSL.8.4]). The compiler realizes it as a
**compiler-synthesized internal rule** whose LHS is `<schema> <binding> where
<pred>` — an ordinary rule `where` clause, evaluated by the same engine that
evaluates every other rule.

This is what makes the single-eval-path guard ([RTIM.14.8]) enforceable rather
than aspirational: the interpreter **must not** run a standalone or parallel
predicate evaluator, and after this realization there is no second evaluator for
it to run. A rule `where` is a network condition, not a free-standing expression
an oracle could point at.

The oracle atom (`OracleEmit`, [RDSC.7.1]) carries `has_where`, and the
interpreter binds it to its synthesized rule by the deterministic name convention
of [RTIM.14.7].

**`where_expr_id` is reserved and unassigned.** The oracle is identified by its
rule, not by an expression reference, so the field has no referent. It is
reserved under [STYL.2.8.7] and never reissued.
